name: A-MEM memory system
relationship_note: The authors distinguish this reusable memory-system repository from the separate AgenticMemory repository used for paper-result reproduction.
learning_signal: New memory content, model-generated context/tags, and similarity to existing notes.
mechanism: Builds structured memory notes, indexes them in ChromaDB, and links or revises related memories as new information arrives. This adapts the external memory organization.
evaluation: The README refers to paper comparisons but directs reproduction work to a different evaluation repository.
limitations: Current library functionality is not proof that the paper’s evaluation has been reproduced. The agent and persistent-memory policy still need application-specific integration.
availability_note: Public reusable memory-library source; package installation documented; not installed or run.
requirements: Python dependencies, ChromaDB/embedding support, and an OpenAI, Ollama, SGLang, or OpenRouter backend as documented.

name: Absolute Zero Reasoner
relationship_note: Official Absolute Zero Reasoner release. The README points to a separate paper branch for original-result replication; the moving development code should not be assumed equivalent.
learning_signal: Python execution validates generated tasks and answers and supplies proposer/solver rewards.
mechanism: Implements reinforced self-play in which a model proposes reasoning tasks and solves them with execution-based verification. Updated weights and a generated task pool support later training iterations.
capabilities: Generate and validate code-based reasoning tasks
Use linked evaluation code, checkpoints, and experiment logs
evaluation: The paper reports coding and mathematics benchmarks; the repository provides training/evaluation resources and distinguishes its paper branch. No checkpoint or training run was tested here.
limitations: The README labels newer development changes as under testing and the raw executor as research-only. Zero newly curated task data does not remove pretraining or engineered supervision.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: GPU training environment with veRL and pretrained weights; documented model-size configurations use multiple 80 GB GPUs. A sandbox executor option requires Docker.

name: ADAS / Meta Agent Search
relationship_note: Official research implementation of Automated Design of Agentic Systems and its Meta Agent Search algorithm; benchmark folders contain separate experiment setups.
learning_signal: Benchmark evaluation and an archive of previously generated agent designs.
mechanism: A fixed meta-agent search procedure writes candidate agent programs, evaluates them, and consults earlier discoveries when proposing new designs. Domain-specific evaluators determine which designs are useful.
capabilities: Retain evaluated discoveries in an archive
Adapt domain-specific search and scoring functions
evaluation: The paper reports task and model transfer experiments; the repository documents how to run the domain studies. No search run was executed here.
limitations: The search procedure is externally configured rather than itself established as an evolving optimizer. The repository explicitly notes that it executes model-generated code.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Python 3.11 environment, required dependencies, model access, and the selected domain’s data and evaluation setup.

name: AFlow
relationship_note: Official standalone AFlow repository, migrated from MetaGPT; it implements the workflow-search method associated with the paper.
learning_signal: Validation-set execution scores and retained search history.
mechanism: Searches code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant over configurable operators. An evaluator scores candidate workflows and guides later prompt and structure changes.
capabilities: Inspect released workflow and validation traces
evaluation: The project provides evaluation code and experiment artifacts for QA, coding, and mathematics tasks; the collection has not rerun them.
limitations: The README warns that some operators may contain migration bugs. Repeated validation use and search cost must be separated from the selected workflow’s test performance and inference cost.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Documented Python 3.9 environment, model configuration, benchmark data, and task operators/evaluator.

name: Agent Lightning v1.0
relationship_note: Official Microsoft agent-training framework. Its v1.0 technical report is linked by the project but is not yet a separate literature entry in this catalog; legacy v0.x is maintained on another branch.
learning_signal: Task rewards and trajectories collected from agents running their existing harnesses.
mechanism: Separates policy training, model-request interception, and agent rollout execution through a trainer, API gateway, and controller. Captured interactions become training samples while the agent retains its tool and control-flow environment.
capabilities: Train policies using real agent harnesses
Collect model interactions through an API gateway
Run rollouts locally or as Kubernetes jobs
evaluation: Project documentation reports search, sandbox, and coding-agent examples. These are project-reported results, not measurements performed or reproduced by this collection.
limitations: This is externally configured training infrastructure, not proof of autonomous self-directed improvement. The v1.0 architecture is a documented refactor, so v0.x installation and experiment assumptions should not be transferred automatically.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: NVIDIA CUDA and a compatible verl/vLLM/PyTorch training stack; current setup docs describe W&B logging and local or Kubernetes rollout environments.

name: Agent Workflow Memory
relationship_note: Author implementation of AWM, with separate Mind2Web and WebArena pipelines.
learning_signal: Annotated training examples in offline mode, or prior action trajectories in online mode.
mechanism: Induces reusable workflow descriptions from example trajectories and supplies them through agent memory. Offline and online pipelines make the source of experience explicit.
evaluation: The README reports web-task results; inspected subdirectory instructions show the offline and online execution paths.
limitations: Web task environments and data must be provisioned separately. The online and offline protocols should not be treated as interchangeable learning evidence.
availability_note: Public research source with environment-specific pipelines; not installed or run.
requirements: Python dependencies, model access, Mind2Web data or WebArena environments, and the documented filtering assets.

name: Agent0
relationship_note: The official repository now hosts the Agent0 series, including a separate vision-language project. This entry describes the Agent0 language-agent subdirectory linked to the cataloged paper.
learning_signal: Curriculum rewards, tool interactions, and self-consistency-filtered executor training data.
mechanism: Alternates curriculum generation, task filtering, and reinforcement-learning updates of a tool-using executor. A deployed code sandbox supplies execution for multi-turn training trajectories.
capabilities: Train an executor through multi-turn RL
evaluation: The paper and repository report reasoning benchmarks for particular trained models. This catalog did not run training or evaluate a released checkpoint.
limitations: Zero data excludes new human-curated task labels, not pretrained weights, reward design, or tools. The documented workflow includes manual checkpoint selection between iterations.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Training-capable hardware, the documented veRL-based environment, pretrained model weights, and a configured SandboxFusion service.

name: Darwin Gödel Machine
relationship_note: Official DGM research code, with separate SWE-bench and Polyglot evaluation components and linked experiment logs; current source was not matched to a paper-run commit.
learning_signal: Coding-benchmark outcomes and logs from candidate agent variants.
mechanism: Runs a coding agent on changes to its own implementation and retains evaluated variants in an archive. Later iterations can build on earlier variants rather than only the most recent agent.
capabilities: Generate and evaluate self-edits to agent code
Maintain an archive of candidate agents
Inspect SWE-bench and Polyglot experiment artifacts
evaluation: The related paper reports coding evaluations and ablations; the repository exposes the research loop and experiment logs. No result was independently reproduced here.
limitations: The outer selection/evaluation process and foundation models remain fixed in the inspected study. The repository executes generated code and is a research implementation, not a validated general deployment service.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Python dependencies, Docker, configured model access, and benchmark environment/data preparation.

name: DSPy
relationship_note: Official DSPy framework; the original paper and GEPA describe particular optimization methods, not every capability of the current release.
learning_signal: Developer-supplied examples and metrics, with feedback or fine-tuning objectives determined by the chosen optimizer.
mechanism: Builds language-model applications from typed signatures and composable Python modules. Optimizers can produce reusable prompts, demonstrations, or tuned model parameters for a supplied task and metric.
capabilities: Compose reasoning, retrieval, and tool-using modules
Optimize instructions and demonstrations against a metric
evaluation: The linked papers report evaluations of specific optimizers; current framework documentation supplies further application examples. This catalog does not test the latest release.
limitations: Optimization must be configured with appropriate data, metrics, and models. A compiled program does not by itself become a continuously self-learning deployed agent.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Python 3.10 or newer, a supported language-model backend, and task examples plus an evaluation metric for optimization.

name: EvoAgentX
relationship_note: Official framework for the EvoAgentX paper; the old EvoAgentX/EvoAgentX URL redirects to ANative-Lab. Current modules can differ from the evaluated paper version.
learning_signal: Task-specific evaluator feedback used by integrated workflow and prompt optimizers.
mechanism: Combines workflow generation, execution, tool integration, and configurable optimization algorithms. Developers can retain optimized workflow definitions and add task-specific evaluators or operators.
capabilities: Generate, save, load, and run agent workflows
Integrate tools and human review points
Apply integrated prompt and workflow optimization
evaluation: The associated paper reports benchmark comparisons; the repository describes an extensible software framework. Neither its feature list nor this inspection reproduces those comparisons.
limitations: Automatic workflow construction is distinct from demonstrated continual learning. Optimizer integrations, task evaluators, and model/tool configurations still determine what can improve.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
license: MIT; bundled MIT notices are included in LICENSE
requirements: Python environment and configured model backend; individual tools can require additional services or execution environments.

name: ExpeL
relationship_note: Official ExpeL implementation; repository availability does not establish reproduction of the paper scores.
learning_signal: Training-task trajectories, success/failure comparisons, and extracted textual insights.
mechanism: Collects agent experiences, extracts reusable natural-language lessons, and retrieves lessons and past examples during later inference. The learned state is external to the model weights.
evaluation: The repository supplies configurations for HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, and WebShop and links the reported study.
limitations: Experience quality and environment feedback shape the extracted insights. Environment setup and current API compatibility were not tested.
availability_note: Public research code with train, insight-extraction, and evaluation entry points; not run.
requirements: Documented Python 3.9 environment, model access, task data, and separate ALFWorld/WebShop setup when used.

name: GEPA
relationship_note: Official GEPA implementation; the current optimize_anything interface broadens the text-artifact optimization scope beyond the paper’s core prompt experiments.
learning_signal: User-defined evaluation scores and diagnostic traces interpreted by a reflection model.
mechanism: Uses reflection over execution feedback to propose textual edits and maintain a population of complementary candidates. Adapters connect the optimizer to prompts, program code, and other text-configured systems.
capabilities: Optimize prompts through DSPy or direct adapters
Track budgets, candidate history, and Pareto-based selection
evaluation: The paper evaluates selected tasks and budgets; project documentation also presents demonstrations and use cases that should be assessed on their own protocols.
limitations: The evaluator and search objective are externally supplied. Wider product examples do not establish the original paper’s results for every adapter or prove autonomous deployment learning.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: A Python environment, a reflection-model backend, an executable evaluation function, and examples or evaluation cases.

name: Hermes Agent
relationship_note: Upstream Hermes application. PAST-Bench studies a Hermes baseline and an experimental Hermes+ variant; this entry is not that benchmark modification or a claim of version equivalence.
learning_signal: Completed task experience, user interaction, periodic memory prompts, and subsequent skill use.
mechanism: Documents a persistent agent loop that creates and revises skills, maintains memory, and searches past sessions. Saved skills and memories remain available across later conversations.
evaluation: Project documentation describes the learning loop; PAST-Bench provides a separate, bounded evaluation of selected Hermes configurations.
limitations: Project feature claims do not establish indefinite improvement or perfect recall. Actual behavior depends on model, settings, task stream, and the inspected version.
availability_note: Public application source with installers and desktop options; not installed or run.
requirements: A supported local/hosted runtime and model-provider connection; optional cloud services have separate costs and terms.

name: HyperAgents
relationship_note: Official HyperAgents implementation accompanying the Hyperagents paper; task-agent and meta-agent code are separate editable components in the released research setup.
learning_signal: Task evaluation and the histories of earlier agent modifications.
mechanism: Makes both a task-solving agent and its improvement procedure editable. A fixed outer loop runs candidate changes and evaluation across configured domains.
capabilities: Inspect released experiment logs and analysis tools
evaluation: The paper reports bounded multi-domain and meta-agent transfer experiments. The repository links experiment logs; no log-level audit or evolution run was performed.
limitations: The outer task/evaluation boundary remains externally specified; this is not evidence of unconstrained improvement. The source is distributed under a noncommercial share-alike license.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Documented Python 3.12 and native build dependencies, Docker, model access, and the chosen domain environment.

name: LangMem
relationship_note: Standalone official memory/optimization library; no matching research paper is asserted in this catalog.
learning_signal: Conversation histories, feedback, and extraction/consolidation prompts.
mechanism: Supplies primitives for storing and consolidating agent experience, plus prompt-refinement tools. Applications can invoke memory operations during interaction or in background processing.
evaluation: The inspected sources provide API examples and integration guidance, not an independently reviewed learning benchmark.
limitations: The quickstart’s in-process store loses data on restart; durable retention requires a database-backed store. Library support alone does not establish a successful learning policy.
availability_note: Public Python package and documentation; not installed or run.
requirements: A supported model provider and storage backend; LangGraph integration is supplied, while functional primitives can use other storage.

name: Letta Code
relationship_note: Current Letta source, succeeding the MemGPT/Letta lineage; the historical letta repository identifies its V1 server as retired. Current behavior is not equivalent to the original MemGPT study.
learning_signal: Conversation experience, explicit user lessons, background reflection, and agent-authored updates.
mechanism: Maintains editable, git-backed memory and agent-scoped skills across conversations. Its documented mods mechanism can extend runtime behavior through locally trusted code.
evaluation: The inspected official material documents mechanisms and user workflows; no learning benchmark of this current harness was independently assessed.
limitations: Persistent edits do not guarantee improved task performance. Mods execute with the runtime’s trust and permissions, and features depend on configuration and host support.
availability_note: Public application/harness source with npm and Python installation routes; not installed or run.
requirements: A supported Node.js or packaged Python installation and configured model access; local, self-hosted, and cloud modes have different requirements.

name: Mem0
relationship_note: Official Mem0 software repository. The current managed-platform algorithm and SDK should not be assumed identical to the earlier paper implementation.
learning_signal: User/agent conversation content and retrieved factual context.
mechanism: Provides memory storage and retrieval for user, session, and agent context through libraries and a server. The managed platform adds functionality beyond the public SDK.
evaluation: The current README explicitly attributes its headline benchmark scores to the managed platform, including proprietary optimizations.
limitations: Those scores cannot be assigned to the open-source SDK unchanged. Factual recall and personalization do not alone establish procedural agent self-improvement.
availability_note: Public SDK/server source and package instructions; hosted service is separate; nothing was installed or run.
requirements: Library dependencies and configured model/embedding/storage backends; the server path uses Docker, while cloud use needs service access.

name: MemRL
relationship_note: Official implementation of MemRL with benchmark entry points; this is not model-weight reinforcement learning.
learning_signal: Environment outcome feedback used to update episodic-memory utility estimates.
mechanism: Combines semantic retrieval with learned utility values on episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Useful experience can therefore influence later retrieval without parameter updates.
evaluation: The README documents HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench evaluation entry points.
limitations: Updating memory utility does not establish that the base model learned new capabilities. Feedback quality and retrieval settings remain part of the evaluated system.
availability_note: Public Python research package with configurations and runners; not installed or run.
requirements: Documented Python 3.10 setup, language-model and embedding endpoints, plus the chosen benchmark assets.

name: ReasoningBank
relationship_note: Official software release for ReasoningBank; supplied task integrations are distinct from a general production agent.
learning_signal: Successful and failed trajectories assessed by model-based correctness judgments.
mechanism: Extracts reasoning lessons from agent trajectories and retrieves them for subsequent tasks. Memory-aware test-time scaling supplies additional experiences for consolidation.
evaluation: The release documents the software-engineering and web-browsing settings used by the paper.
limitations: The agent judges its own trajectories in parts of the workflow. Current default-branch code and provider configurations were not independently reproduced.
availability_note: Public research source with task-specific agent and evaluation directories; not run.
requirements: Python dependencies, supported model-provider access, and benchmark environments; WebArena setup includes BrowserGym and Docker.

name: SEAL
relationship_note: Official Self-Adapting Language Models code, with separate general-knowledge and few-shot study directories; it is an adaptation research framework rather than a general agent application.
learning_signal: Performance measured after applying a generated self-edit to model parameters.
mechanism: Trains a model to generate adaptation data or update directives, then evaluates the gradient-based adaptation produced by those edits. The knowledge-incorporation implementation uses temporary LoRA training and evaluation to score candidate edits.
evaluation: The paper reports knowledge and ARC adaptation studies, including retention tests. The repository contains code, data, and study documentation; these were not executed here.
limitations: The related study still observes forgetting, and evaluating edits involves actual model training. The release should not be treated as a stable lifelong-learning service.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Python 3.12 and training dependencies; the README describes experiments using two A100/H100 GPUs and requires adapting provided SLURM directives to the execution environment.

name: Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA)
relationship_note: Official experiment code for A Self-Improving Coding Agent; current repository behavior was not independently matched to the exact paper evaluation revision.
learning_signal: Configured benchmark scores and archived results from preceding agent versions.
mechanism: Alternates evaluating a coding agent, storing its results, and asking it to improve its own codebase. The next iteration uses the modified implementation.
capabilities: Inspect event traces in a local execution viewer
evaluation: The paper reports selected coding and synthetic-task experiments; the repository provides loop configuration and trace inspection. No benchmark was run for this catalog.
limitations: The repository recommends its Docker environment because the agent can run shell commands. It also identifies run variance and benchmark realism as open work; gains need not transfer beyond the selected tasks.
availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
requirements: Docker, local Python dependencies, a configured supported model provider, and chosen benchmark resources.

name: SkillRL
relationship_note: Official training code and linked checkpoints for SkillRL; repository licensing does not determine every linked model or dataset license.
learning_signal: Successful/failed trajectories, distillation data, and validation failures during reinforcement learning.
mechanism: Distills experience into a hierarchical SkillBank and trains an agent policy with retrieved skills. Skill updates and model-parameter learning occur together in the training workflow.
evaluation: The repository links SFT/RL checkpoints and documents ALFWorld, WebShop, and search training paths.
limitations: This is a training stack, not a training-free memory plug-in. Checkpoint availability and source inspection do not reproduce the reported comparisons.
availability_note: Public training source; model and dataset links are provided by the maintainers but were not downloaded.
requirements: GPU-capable training setup with the documented vLLM/FlashAttention stack, task environments, model checkpoints, and configured provider access.

name: Voyager
relationship_note: Official research implementation of Voyager; the current checkout was not matched to a paper experiment commit.
learning_signal: Minecraft observations, execution errors, and model-based task verification.
mechanism: Explores Minecraft with an automatic curriculum and accumulates executable skills. Retrieved skills and iterative program repair support later tasks without fine-tuning the language model.
evaluation: The README reports exploration and new-world skill-reuse experiments from the associated study.
limitations: The environment uses Minecraft and supplied control APIs. Model-based verification and retained programs are not guaranteed correct; no experiment was reproduced here.
availability_note: Public research source with setup instructions and a skill library; not installed or run.
requirements: Python 3.9+, Node.js 16.13+, Minecraft with the documented mods, and a supported model API configuration.
